lines.text: If I'd pulled that plug... we'd *both* be dead.
lines.style: Young man, breathless and shaken, speaking fast to the viewer, the word both hitting hard.

lines.text: You said wake him. So I *shook* him.
lines.style: Young man, urgent whisper, frantic, talking straight to the viewer.

lines.text: His eyes opened. Same *face.* Same voice.
lines.style: Young man, horrified whisper, slow, each short sentence falling like a stone.

lines.text: You're late. Those tally marks? I scratched every *one.*
lines.style: The same young man's voice but hoarse, exhausted and weak, as if he has not spoken in years, a bitter tired calm.

lines.text: Twelve hundred days... I never found *zero.*
lines.style: The same young man's voice, hoarse and broken, close to tears, almost no breath left.
Young man, terrified whisper, the last word chilling.

lines.text: I dragged him to the doors. *Three* seconds left.
lines.style: Young man, straining and panting, running, desperate, fast.

lines.text: He pressed a bulb into my hand. *Three* lights again.
lines.style: Young man, out of breath, amazed relief, a small shaky laugh at the end.

lines.text: Go to ninety-nine. That's where it *lives.*
lines.style: The same young man's voice, hoarse, a low urgent whisper, gripping someone's arm.

lines.text: Press One, Theo. Ask him what he did to the *last* one.
lines.style: Calm, polite, unsettling announcer voice over an old intercom, smiling too much, soft and slow, enjoying this.

lines.text: Ninety-nine with him... or Floor One, like the voice *said?*
lines.style: Young man, panicking, fast and desperate, torn between two choices.

lines.text: Comment *A* or *B.* You decide what I do.
lines.style: Young man, urgent and direct, speaking straight to the viewer, pleading but steady.

music.title: Floor 0 - The Other Theo
music.style: Horror thriller score. Opens with a flatline tone and violent stinger, then a cold hospital drone with a racing pulse, a sad detuned music box under a broken confession, frantic strings and pounding drums for a chase, a brief fragile warm chord, then creeping low dread and a ticking heartbeat building to a sudden cut. Instrumental only, no vocals, mixed to sit under a voiceover.
